Let $u=3x-2.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u.
$$

We now write our integral in terms of $u,$ calculate the integral as normal, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ at the very end:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 48(3x-2)^{7}\,\text{d}x & =\int 48{u}^{7}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =48\cdot \frac{1}{3}\int {u}^{7}\,\text{d}u \\  & =16\cdot \frac{{u}^{8}}{8}+C \\  & =2\cdot {u}^{8}+C \\  & =2(3x-2)^{8}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's double-check that our result is correct. If we differentiate the result, then it should come out to the original integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[2(3x-2)^{8}+C] & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[2(3x-2)^{8}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =16(3x-2)^{7}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3x-2)+0 \\  & =16(3x-2)^{7}\cdot 3 \\  & =48(3x-2)^{7}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
